# AuthLayout

The page for signing in, signing up or resetting a password: one `Card` in the middle of the screen, with your brand, the title as the page's `<h1>`, the form, and a line under the card. It is the page's `<main>`, at least as tall as the screen, and fills a phone's width.

```tsx
import { AuthLayout } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/auth-layout/auth-layout";
```

## Example

```tsx
<AuthLayout title="Sign in" description="Welcome back." footer={<Link href="/signup">Create an account</Link>}>
  <Form>
    <TextField label="Email" name="email" type="email" required />
    <Button type="submit" fullWidth>Sign in</Button>
  </Form>
</AuthLayout>
```

## Usage

Use `Dialog` for a sign-in prompt over another page.

## Use instead when

- Use `SidebarLayout` or `StackedLayout` instead for the signed-in app.

## Props

Type: `AuthLayoutProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `ReactNode` |  | Your logo or product name, above the title. Link it to the home page. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The form: fields and the submit button, usually a `Form`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins and height (`min-h-96`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the title: "Welcome back to Spoonjoy." |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the card, such as the link to the other form: "No account? Sign up". |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The page's heading, its `<h1>`: "Sign in". |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `heading`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `title`: `<AuthLayout title="Sign in">`.
- `logo`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `brand`: `<AuthLayout brand={<Logo />}>`.
- `subtitle`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `description`: `<AuthLayout description="Welcome back">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
